Belgium

28 ads · €7429 spend · 225 purchases
✅ What's Working
• WCDxBA concept is the hidden gem: #5 at 10.3x, #1 at 5.11x, #2 at 3.45x — all profitable across variants yet starved of budget.
• Carousel and conversational formats outperform polished statics: Carousel copy hits 4.23x ROAS with €19.89 CPP, iMessage #2 delivers 4.01x — native-feeling creative converts.
• Summer #2 is the volume workhorse: 65 purchases at 4.48x ROAS, proving seasonal lifestyle positioning sells in Belgium.
❌ What's Not Working
• Solitaire concept is a budget drain: #1 burned €917 at 1.59x, #2 spent €91 with zero purchases — €1,008 wasted on a dead concept.
• Split concept fails consistently: #1 at 0.66x (€121 CPP) and #2 at 1.86x — neither variant justifies continued spend.
• Catalog statics don't convert: #1 and #2 combined spent €153 for one single purchase — the format is broken for this audience.
⬆ Double Down On
• WCDxBA in every format: 3/3 variants are profitable, ROAS ranges 3.45x–10.3x, and total spend is only €325. This concept has massive scaling headroom.
• Carousel and native/conversational formats: the Carousel and iMessage creatives punch well above their weight — replicate these formats for other product lines.
• Video creative: Video General #3 (4.12x) and Video Creative #2 (7.08x) both outperform most statics, yet only €304 total is allocated to video. The format is severely underinvested.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Solitaire — both variants failed, €1,008 gone. Stop all Solitaire statics immediately.
• Catalog statics — zero evidence this format works. €153 spent, one purchase total. Dead.
• Split concept — neither variant cracks 2x ROAS on €783 combined spend. Retire it.

🇩🇪

Germany

2 ads · €206 spend · 2 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Both video ads generate unusually high CTRs (155%+ and 214%), meaning the creative hooks grab attention effectively in the German market.
• Video format is clearly engaging for this audience — both Stack and Kay concepts drive clicks, proving the product visuals resonate at top-of-funnel.
• Two different product concepts (Stack, Kay) both generated at least 1 purchase each on modest spend, confirming baseline demand exists in DE.
❌ What's Not Working
• Both "Video _ Stack #1" (ROAS 0.8x) and "Video _ Kay #1" (ROAS 0.67x) are burning cash — sub-1x ROAS means every euro spent loses money.
• Massive CTR-to-purchase gap signals a brutal post-click breakdown: likely non-localized landing pages, no German-language trust signals, or price friction for DE shoppers.
• Only 2 ads in the entire DE market with zero format diversity (no Static, no UGC) — this is not a real test, it's a coin flip with no learning structure.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce German-language creative immediately — DE consumers expect native-language ads; English-only video is a conversion killer for affordable luxury.
• Lean into UGC with German creators — social proof in the local language will bridge the trust gap that's clearly destroying post-click conversion.
• Test static carousel and collection ads featuring price anchoring (e.g., 'Ab €49') to combat price objection and reduce CPP below €50.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running English-only video ads in Germany and expecting conversions. The CTR proves interest; the ROAS proves the funnel is broken.
• Stop treating DE as a copy-paste of BE/NL — this market needs its own localized creative strategy, not recycled assets.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €2969 spend · 1261 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Urgency/last-call statics are untouchable: 'Last Call #1 - Copy' hits 85.75x ROAS at €0.62 CPP, 'Last Call #1' at 67.47x, 'Last Call #2' at 50.53x — scarcity is this account's superpower.
• Value/price-math statics convert hard: 'Waar vo #1 - Copy' (47.42x ROAS), 'Berekening #2' (43.38x) prove rational price justification crushes emotional storytelling for this audience.
• Artist-specific statics outperform generic: 'Static _ RUBEN' (30.23x ROAS, €2.32 CPP) shows named talent drives ticket action far better than mood-based creative.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ Organic #1' is literally losing money: 0.94x ROAS, €36.68 CPP — 2 purchases on €73 spend is an active disaster still running.
• 'Video _ Aftermovie #1' proves the video-first assumption is dead wrong for conversions: 7 purchases at €12.95 CPP while statics average ~€2 CPP — a 6x efficiency gap.
• The client belief that creative should be video-first is contradicted by every single data point — all 18 top-performing ads are statics.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more urgency/scarcity statics: 'Last Call' variants, ticket-count countdowns, 'bijna uitverkocht' angles — this is the #1 conversion lever by a mile.
• Expand price-math/value statics: more 'Berekening' and 'Waar vo' style rational breakdowns showing cost-per-hour, comparison to nights out, group savings.
• Build an artist spotlight static series using the RUBEN template for every confirmed headliner on the lineup — proven formula, just swap the name.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill 'Static _ Organic #1' immediately — sub-1x ROAS is paying Meta to lose money.
• Stop running aftermovie video in conversion campaigns — €12.95 CPP cannot compete with €0.62-€3 static CPPs, not even close.
• Abandon the 'video-first' creative strategy for purchase-optimized campaigns — this account is a static account, full stop.

Belgium

30 ads · €8373 spend · 224 results
✅ What's Working
• Comparison ('Vergelijking') statics dominate — the two best 'Vergelijking #1 - Copy' variants deliver 70 combined leads at €24-27 CPR, proving the broker-vs-fixed-fee savings angle is the account's growth engine.
• 'Static _ Smart #1 - Copy' (€334 variant) is the account MVP at €18.53 CPR with 18 leads — punchy, efficient, and under-scaled.
• Copy iterations systematically crush originals: 'Vergelijking #1 - Copy' at €24 CPR vs 'Vergelijking #1' original at €83 CPR. Creative refreshes are unlocking serious efficiency gains.
❌ What's Not Working
• Authority/press angles are expensive dead ends — 'Static _ De Tijd 2' burned €199 for a single lead. Credibility framing doesn't convert cold feed traffic.
• Testimonial and product creatives flopping hard — 'Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy' at €75 CPR and 'Product #2 - Copy' at €100 CPR suggest social proof and feature-led hooks need a complete rethink.
• Poll format is unreliable — 'Poll #2 - Copy 2' spent €169 with zero results. High CTR, no conversions = engagement bait that doesn't translate to leads.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3-4 new Vergelijking variants with different savings scenarios, property price ranges, and visual layouts — this comparison angle is proven and far from fatigued.
• Scale and iterate on the 'Smart' format — the €18.53 CPR winner is begging for siblings testing different USP hooks (zero-risk, 40% more buyers, Immoweb reach).
• Launch a dedicated FR-language creative sprint — top performers appear NL-focused. Mirror winning Vergelijking and Smart concepts in French to unlock Wallonia/Brussels volume.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill 'Static _ De Tijd 2' immediately — €199 per lead is 8x your best performers. Press credibility is not a cold-traffic hook.
• Kill 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' and the zero-result 'Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' variant — both burned triple-digit budgets producing nothing.
• Kill 'Static _ Thomas Guenter #2 - Copy' and 'Product #2 - Copy' — testimonial and product-feature angles are bleeding money at €75-100 CPR.

• Renée #1 - Copy is actively losing money: 0.67x ROAS, €107 CPP on €215 spend—wrong creator fit, wrong angle, or both
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce product-hero statics for every SKU (Helbo, Selva Snow, sunglasses) mirroring the Ziris #2 format that hit 4.22x—simple product focus with clean creative converts best
• Scale lifestyle and colorway statics: shoot more variants of Colors and Lifestyle angles with different models, settings, and colorways—these consistently deliver 3.5x+ ROAS
• Create USP-driven creatives around prescription lenses ('op sterkte') and photochromic tech—these are your key differentiators vs Oakley and Decathlon and zero ads currently leverage them

• Cycling-specific seasonal hooks outperform generic product-beauty shots in this market.
❌ What's Not Working
• Total NL spend is only ~€119 across 10 ads in 30 days — budget is spread far too thin for the algorithm to learn anything. Seven ads got under €10 each.

• Non-sport-contextual creatives like 'Static _ Colors #1/#2' and generic 'Static _ Split' ads have zero conversions and near-zero meaningful delivery — product-beauty-only doesn't sell to Dutch cyclists.
⬆ Double Down On
• More split-format cycling creatives with seasonal or race-event hooks (post-Vuelta, fall riding season, CX season) — this is the only proven pattern.
• Lead with the 'op sterkte' (prescription) differentiator — it's the #1 reason a Dutch cyclist picks NAOS over Oakley/Decathlon and it appears in zero current ads.
• Photochromic lens benefit storytelling — Dutch weather is famously changeable; show the lens adapting from clouds to sun on a real ride.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running 10 static ads on ~€120/month. Consolidate to 3-4 max so Meta can actually optimize. This account is in permanent learning-limited hell.
• Kill all generic product-on-background creatives ('Colors', 'Lumitron') that lack a sport context or clear value proposition — they get no traction in NL.
• Stop duplicating Split #1/#2 variants without meaningful creative differences; the losing variant just cannibalizes budget.

🇧🇪

Belgium

15 ads · €2443 spend · 149 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Catalog Carousel - Espresso Coffee is the undisputed workhorse: €1100 spend, 90 purchases, 39.44x ROAS, and a €12.22 CPP — product-feed carousels with espresso framing clearly convert.
• Short-form video with origin storytelling punches above its weight: Video _ XPL04 MG #2 delivered 39.25x ROAS at just €9.07 CPP on minimal spend — the MG origin angle resonates deeply.
• Static_Barista_Courses - Copy is a sleeper hit: 34.94x ROAS and €15.05 CPP — education/barista culture as a hook drives high-intent clicks and purchases.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static _ Origin #1 is the biggest misfire: €139 spent, only 2 purchases, 4.1x ROAS, €69.62 CPP — the origin story execution here is flat and not landing despite the brand's USP.
• Video _ XPL04 KA variants (#1 and #2) underperform: combined €81 spend, only 1 purchase — the KA origin creative doesn't resonate compared to MG.
• Low-spend statics (Barista #1, General #1, Quality #1) got almost no delivery and zero purchases — Meta's algorithm deprioritized them, signaling weak creative signals.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-feed carousels segmented by use case (espresso, filter, subscription bundles) — the catalog format is proven, replicate it across product lines.
• Short-form video origin stories using the MG creative style — authentic, specific, and emotionally connecting sourcing to the cup.
• Barista education / course-adjacent hooks in static and video — the 'learn like a barista' angle converts and differentiates from generic DTC coffee ads.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the KA origin video variants — two creatives, €81 spent, 1 purchase total. The story or execution isn't connecting.
• Kill Static _ Origin #1 — worst CPP in the account at €69.62. Origin storytelling works in video (MG), not in this static execution.
• Stop running statics with under €10 spend and no signal (Barista #1, General #1, Quality #1) — they're dead on arrival, rethink the hooks before relaunching.

Belgium

4 ads · €884 spend · 68 results
✅ What's Working
• "Static _ Investeren _ 2" is a lead-gen machine — 68 results at €12.85 CPL is excellent for Belgian real estate. Meta clearly favors this variant.
• Investment angle resonates with the Belgian audience — the only angle tested, and it's delivering volume at low cost.
• Static format is proving sufficient for conversion when the message is right — no need for complex production to generate leads.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero creative diversity — all 4 ads are static investment variants. No lifestyle, no second-home, no kijkwoning angle. You're leaving entire buyer segments untouched.
• "Static _ Investeren _ 3", "Static _ Investeren _ 4", and "Static _ Investeren" got crushed in the auction by variant 2 — combined €11 spend, zero results. They're dead weight.
• No video, no carousel, no motion — for a waterfront property with panoramic Westerschelde views, you're criminally underusing the visual story.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more investment-angle creatives with fresh visuals and copy iterations — variant 2 proves the thesis, now test new hooks around 100% huurgarantie and fossil-free USPs.
• Launch lifestyle/emotional creatives — drone footage of the Westerschelde, golden-hour water reflections, the rust-en-ruimte promise. Belgian second-home buyers need to feel it, not just calculate it.
• Create dedicated kijkwoning visit creatives — the brief says drive visits, but no ad is explicitly doing that. Use urgency and exclusivity to pull people across the border.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running 4 near-identical static investment ads against each other — Meta will always pick a winner and starve the rest. Differentiate angles or kill the losers.
• Stop ignoring video and motion formats for a waterfront lifestyle product — this is malpractice for real estate creative in 2024.

• "Static _ Water Wind _ Form" is the engine: 61 leads at €18.34 CPR with the highest spend — emotional, evocative water/wind imagery clearly resonates with Dutch buyers.

• Dreamy, nature-forward creative crushes direct investment messaging on every metric.
❌ What's Not Working
• The "Investeren" angle is struggling across the board — variant 2 costs 2x per lead (€38.04), variants 3, 4, and original generated zero results combined on €32 total spend.
• Too many near-identical "Investeren" copy variants (4 versions) diluting budget with no meaningful creative differentiation — Meta's algorithm starved them for a reason.
• Zero video diversity — only one video ad running despite it showing the best engagement signal in the account.
⬆ Double Down On
• Atmospheric lifestyle statics: replicate the Water Wind formula — evocative nature imagery (Westerschelde, polder light, tides) with minimal text and form-based lead capture.
• Video content at scale: produce 3-4 new lifestyle videos exploring seasons, golden hour on the dike, interior walkthrough — the format is underexploited and outperforming.
• Experiential "kom kijken" creative: leverage kijkwoning/kijkappartementen availability as a soft CTA — invite, don't sell.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill "Static _ Investeren _ 3 - Copy" and "Static _ Investeren _ 4 - Copy" immediately — zero results, lowest CTRs, Meta already buried them.
• Stop producing more copy-paste investment statics — four variants of the same angle with no winner beyond variant 2 is a creative dead end.
• Stop treating investment messaging as a standalone hook — fold rental guarantee into lifestyle-first creative instead.

Other

18 ads · €4198 spend · 347 results
✅ What's Working
• Evocative water/nature imagery + instant form combo is the engine — "Water Wind _ Form" delivers 165 leads at €8.19 with massive spend, proving lifestyle-first creative scales in this market.
• Visit-oriented CTAs convert efficiently when refined — "Visit #2 - Copy" pulls 64 leads at €8.51, outperforming Visit #1 by 3x on efficiency, showing iteration pays off.
• New apartment product-specific messaging wins — "Nieuw_App #1" delivers the second-lowest CPL at €7.50 with 18 results on minimal budget, a clear scaling candidate.
❌ What's Not Working
• Social proof falls flat at scale — "Review _ Form" ate €696 but CPL ballooned to €30.25, suggesting testimonials don't move the needle for aspirational waterfront property buyers.
• Copy duplicates of winners consistently underperform — "Water Wind _ Form - Copy" (€38.27 CPL) and "Nieuw_App #1 - Copy" (€25.03 CPL) prove that cloning without meaningful iteration is wasted budget.
• List-format "Opsomming" ads are inconsistent — #2 spent €467 at €27.46 CPL while #3 got zero results on €14 spend; rational feature dumps don't match the dreamy brand positioning.
⬆ Double Down On
• Atmospheric water/wind/nature visuals paired with instant lead forms — this is your proven formula. Produce 3-4 new variants with different waterfront moments (sunrise, storm, golden hour, sailing).
• Product-specific angles (apartments, hotel apartments with rental guarantee) with low-friction CTAs — "Nieuw_App" proves that when you name the product clearly, qualified leads come cheaper.
• Visit/kijkwoning-focused creatives with refined lifestyle hooks — Visit #2's success shows this CTA converts; pair it with new hero imagery and urgency messaging.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop duplicating winning ads without meaningful creative changes — both "- Copy" variants tanked. Change the hook, visual, or CTA or don't bother.
• Pause all Opsomming (list/bullet) formats — rational feature dumps contradict the dreamy positioning and underperform across the board.
• Stop spending on "Review _ Form" at current CPL — €696 for 23 leads at €30.25 each is 3.7x worse than your best performer.

Belgium

12 ads · €1712 spend · 280 results
✅ What's Working
• Bauhaus creative series dominates spend allocation and delivers consistently — Bauhaus #5 (€528, 75 results at €7.04) and Bauhaus #2 (€111, 22 results at €5.07) prove the Bauhaus aesthetic resonates with this affluent audience.
• Naoshima #2 is the efficiency leader at €5.62/result with 79 results on €444 spend — the Japanese minimalist architecture angle clearly pulls qualified clicks.
• Cost per result across top performers sits at an exceptional €4-7 range for luxury real estate leads — the architecture-as-brand-identity positioning is working hard across all three naming conventions (Bauhaus, Naoshima, Sommerfeld).
❌ What's Not Working
• Bauhaus #4 is a budget black hole — €20 spent, 1 lonely result at €20.38 CPR, nearly 4x the average. The creative is broken despite the Bauhaus naming convention working elsewhere.
• Naoshima #1, #3 and Sommerfeld #1 collectively spent €9 with zero results — Meta's algorithm already starved them of budget, which tells you everything. These are dead on arrival.
• CTRs above 300% across the board suggest 'results' are likely engagement or landing page views, not true leads — if these are optimized for anything lighter than form fills, the entire campaign may be generating vanity metrics, not pipeline.
⬆ Double Down On
• Bauhaus visual language is the clear winner — produce more static variants in this aesthetic (clean lines, white/concrete tones, modernist geometry). Bauhaus #1, #2, #5 all deliver.
• Naoshima's Japanese-minimalist-meets-Belgian-coast angle is a differentiator — expand this series with new property shots and lifestyle framing. Only one variant (#2) got real budget; there's headroom.
• Sommerfeld #2 quietly delivered the lowest CPR in the set (€4.19) on minimal spend — this creative direction deserves a proper budget test before being overlooked.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill Naoshima #1, Naoshima #3, and Sommerfeld #1 immediately — zero results, negligible spend, Meta's own algorithm already rejected them. Don't resuscitate.
• Kill Bauhaus #4 — €20.38 CPR is unacceptable when siblings in the same series deliver at €5-7. The creative is the problem, not the audience.

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

17 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🇧🇪

Belgium

17 ads · €2497 spend · 92 results
✅ What's Working
• Moment-based B2B creative dominates: "4 Momenten #1" delivers 30 results at €15.76 each — best efficiency-at-volume in the account by far.
• Specific venue/use-case framing converts: "Açai Koffiebar" (23 results) and "Upgrade Brunch" (8 results) prove that showing B2B prospects exactly where açai fits their business drives action.
• "Geen excuus #1" quietly crushes at €10.09/result with a 239.82% CTR — objection-handling copy clearly resonates but has barely been given budget (€30).
❌ What's Not Working
• "Boost" messaging is a money pit: "Boost #2" burned €393 for just 5 results (€78.63 each) and "Boost #1" isn't much better at €36.04 — vague "boost" framing gives B2B prospects no concrete reason to act.
• Consumer-facing creatives are dead on arrival: "Bowl #1" (€128) and "Nutri A #2" (€104) generated zero results — without a webshop to convert, these awareness statics have no measurable endpoint and are leaking budget.
• Multiple #2 variants across ad sets ("Snel #2", "Geen excuus #2", "4 Momenten #2", "Drinks #2") are starved of spend and producing nothing — Meta's algorithm is picking winners fast and burying the rest, so these are just clutter.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more moment/occasion-specific B2B statics: "4 Momenten" and "Koffiebar" prove that when you name the exact business context (brunch menu, coffee bar add-on, post-workout juice bar), cost/result drops dramatically. Create variants for lunch service, dessert menus, and catering.
• Lean into objection-handling copy: "Geen excuus #1" at €10.09/result signals that addressing barriers (complexity, prep time, cost) directly in the headline is the highest-efficiency angle — build a full series around common B2B objections.
• Shift consumer-facing budget into B2B retail activation content: since there's no webshop, create B2B statics specifically for retail category managers at Bio-Planet/Delhaize showing sell-through data, shelf positioning, and consumer demand signals rather than running brand awareness statics into a void.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill both "Boost" creatives immediately — combined €537 spent at an average €52.34/result, nearly 3.5x worse than the account's best performers. The messaging is too generic for a B2B audience that needs practical reasons to stock açai.
• Kill "Bowl #1" and "Nutri A #2" — €232 in combined spend with zero results. Consumer statics without a conversion endpoint are pure waste on Meta. If consumer awareness is the goal, reallocate to Google where the primary channel already lives.
• Stop launching #2 variants that Meta's algorithm immediately deprioritizes — seven ads have under €15 spend with zero results. Consolidate creative energy into fewer, stronger concepts rather than diluting with weak alternates.

Other

19 ads · €558 spend · 1 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Instagram post: New deliveries! Bekijk ons gamma..." is the only converter at 10.66x ROAS — product-focused 'new arrivals' messaging with a clear CTA works.
• Posts with specific seasonal or product hooks ("It's thé time of thé season", "shop online", "Product in de kijker") generate the highest engagement CTRs (400-636%).
• Dutch-language copy with product urgency outperforms vague emoji-only or empty-caption posts.
❌ What's Not Working
• 18 of 19 ads produced zero purchases — €479 wasted on boosted posts with no conversion optimization. Generic "Instagram-bericht" ads (€106, €11, €3, €1) have zero sales strategy.
• Empty or emoji-only captions ("Bericht: ''" x3, "Instagram-bericht: ❤️") burn €106 combined with nothing to show — no CTA, no product info, no reason to buy.
• Budget is atomized across 19 ads averaging €29 each — no single ad gets enough spend to optimize or learn.
⬆ Double Down On
• 'New arrivals / new deliveries' product showcase ads with clear CTAs and pricing — the only proven converter pattern.
• Consolidate budget into 3-4 proper conversion-optimized campaigns instead of boosting random Instagram posts.
• Dutch-language copy with specific product callouts, seasonal urgency, and a direct shop link — mirror the winning ad's structure.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop boosting random Instagram posts with no caption, no CTA, and no product focus — they're vanity metrics factories.
• Stop spreading €559/month across 19 ads. Consolidate into max 4-5 ads with proper conversion objectives.
• Kill emoji-only captions and posts without a clear path to purchase.

30 ads · €4225 spend · 4 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Video _ Call #2 - Copy" is the only real winner: 2 purchases at €35 CPP — call/booking format clearly resonates.
• Personal-name creatives convert: "Static _ Matthias #1" drove a purchase at €110 CPP, suggesting social proof from real people moves the needle.
• Video formats with direct engagement hooks (Call, DM) outperform polished Concierge and static Business ads on conversion.
❌ What's Not Working
• Static Business ads are a budget bonfire: "Static _ Business #1 - Copy" (€785) and "Static _ Business #3" (€692) burned €1,477 combined with zero purchases.
• The entire Concierge video series (6 variants, €842 total) produced exactly zero purchases — the concept is dead.
• "Static _ Review #1 - Copy" spent €509 with no conversions — social proof in this format is not landing.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Video _ Call variations — the booking/call CTA is the only proven conversion driver at a viable CPP.
• Lean into named-person / real-testimonial creatives like the Matthias approach — authenticity over corporate polish.
• Test direct-response video formats (DM, Call) with stronger hooks and urgency — the funnel works, the top-of-funnel needs sharpening.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Static _ Business creatives immediately — €1,668 burned across 4 variants with zero results.
• Kill the entire Concierge video series — 6 ads, €842 spent, zero signal, the concept is a proven loser.
• Kill "Static _ Review #1 - Copy" — €509 for nothing; this review format doesn't convert.

Other

30 ads · €8779 spend · 147 results
✅ What's Working
• Vottem is the standout project — every format delivers (Vottem_apt €17.18/result, Vottem_video €18.80, Vottem_logements €22.21, Vottem_animatie €33.73). Video and animation formats drive highest CTR and lowest CPR across the board.
• Brugge_penthouse is a volume machine at €33.25/result with 24 conversions and the highest CTR in the account (355.74%). Proof that premium property + strong creative = efficient lead gen.
• Exterior/architectural visuals outperform interior shots — Blom_ext_cta (€36.92) and west_ext (€54.28) both deliver where interior-focused stokerie_int_v2 (€113.64) flops.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is a black hole — slideshow burned €453 with zero results, reel got 2 at €164.93, remarketing got 1 at €166.03. The project or creative approach is fundamentally broken.
• Charleroi_te-huur at €170.79/result and Charleroi_native at €105.37 show this market/project has a demand or targeting problem. Neither format rescues it.
• Georges ads suffer from weak CTR (65-75%) and middling CPR despite multiple CTA variants — the creative itself isn't compelling enough to drive action.
⬆ Double Down On
• Replicate the Vottem playbook (video + animation + apartment-specific messaging) for other projects. This project alone accounts for 53 results at sub-€25 CPR.
• Lean into motion formats — video and animation consistently halve CPR vs. static/slideshow across Vottem, west, and Brugge.
• Exterior-first creative with strong architectural framing (Blom_ext_cta, west_ext, Brugge_penthouse) consistently beats interior or generic imagery.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Wildebeek spend immediately — three formats, €949 total, 3 results. No creative can fix what looks like a project-market fit problem.
• Kill Charleroi_te-huur — €342 for 2 results, 53% CTR is the worst in the account. Rental messaging is not converting.
• Kill stokerie_int_v2 — €227 for 2 results, interior-focused creative is losing to terras/exterior versions of the same project.

Other

3 ads · €303 spend · 5 results
✅ What's Working
• Product-specific naming wins: "PVC. VER.- PUB CONVERTION - 2026" delivers €29.92 CPR vs €65.98 for the broader "PERGOLAS" ad — specificity cuts cost by 55%.
• The "2026" forward-planning angle appears in both converting ads, suggesting prospects respond to future-project framing.
• Sky-high CTRs across all three ads (128-198%) indicate strong thumb-stopping creative — the hook is working, but conversion follow-through is weak.
❌ What's Not Working
• "VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" has zero results on €9 spend and no "2026" hook — generic product name with no urgency = dead weight.
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - 2026" eats 88% of budget but delivers €66 leads — volume without efficiency is just burning cash.
• No ROAS data on any ad means either tracking is broken or the funnel downstream is a black hole — this is the real emergency.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product-specific ads à la "PVC. VER." — replicate this narrow-focus approach for each product line (pergolas, verandas, insulation) individually.
• The "2026 project planning" angle is a clear psychological trigger — build an entire creative series around "Plan your 2026 outdoor space now" with seasonal urgency layered on.
• High CTR proves the visual creative grabs attention — pair it with stronger landing page alignment and lead form optimization to convert those clicks into actual results.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the generic "VERANDAS" ad immediately — no results, no differentiator, no reason to exist.
• Stop running any ad without conversion tracking properly firing — fix ROAS measurement before scaling a single euro more.

✅ What's Working
• "CARPORTS" is the clear winner: 7 results at €8.46 each on just €59 spend — strong signal that carport demand is real and converting cheaply.
• "PERGOLAS - PUB CONVERTIONS" generates results at €18.36 — viable but at 2x the cost of carports, suggesting pergola interest exists but creative or audience needs tightening.

• The overall account spend is tiny (€118 total) — this business is massively under-investing in a high-ticket product category where one veranda sale could fund months of ad spend.
⬆ Double Down On
• Carport-specific creative: this is the cheapest result generator — build a full creative suite around carports (before/after, seasonal urgency, aluminum vs. wood).
• Product-specific landing pages per ad set: carports, pergolas, and verandas each need dedicated conversion paths — generic pages kill conversion rates.
• Social proof and project showcase creative: high-ticket outdoor construction buyers need trust — show completed local projects in Colmar/Liège with customer testimonials.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running conversion campaigns at €2 budgets — it's mathematically impossible to exit learning phase. Either fund them properly (€20+/day) or don't run them.
• Stop ignoring ROAS tracking — install conversion value tracking immediately or you'll never know which product line actually drives revenue.

⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more general/brand-level creatives following the "Algemeen - Visual" formula: multi-domain, aspirational, not dependent on a single creator face.
• Create short highlight reels compiling the best visuals across all domains — the data says breadth sells better than depth for this audience.
• Lean into Duinpanne as the hero location in new creative; it's the only domain that converted affordably when paired with a creator.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop funding single-creator x single-location ads that have delivered ≤1 result each — Janneke-Gavers, TheLifePlanFamily-Palingbeek, and Magnolia-Raversyde are burning public money.
• Kill the current GIF creative or relaunch it immediately; sitting at €0 spend it's dead weight in the account.
• Abandon the assumption that influencer names drive conversions — the nameless "Algemeen" ad outperforms every creator ad by 3-16x on cost/result.

13 ads · Meta · last 30 days

🌐

Other

13 ads · €560 spend · 9 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Person-named Reels are the ONLY format generating purchases — 'Post
• Reel Merlene' at 5.58x ROAS and €12.09 CPP is a standout winner on tiny spend.
• Product-specific Reels (named items like Merlene, Shay, Marie Jo) outperform generic text posts across the board — the format itself is the differentiator.
• Low-budget Reels convert more efficiently than higher-spend static posts — €24 on Merlene outperformed €196 on Mary-Lynn in ROAS by 13x.
❌ What's Not Working
• Every single 'Bericht' (static text post) ad has ZERO purchases despite €274+ combined spend — 'Coole, comfy styles' (€90), 'Deze week kan je hier terecht!' (€90 across two), and 'We starten de week' (€75) are pure waste.
• Event-format ads ('XXL STOCK SALE!', 'Feestelijke opening Lokeren') generated zero conversions — awareness-only messaging doesn't convert on Meta for this brand.
• 'Post
• Reel Mary-Lynn' ate the biggest budget (€196) but returned only 0.41x ROAS — something about this creative (product, hook, or audience) is fundamentally broken despite driving 7 purchases.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more person/product-named Reel content in the Merlene mold — short, product-focused, low-friction. This is the only proven conversion format.
• Shift ALL budget away from static Bericht posts and into Reel-first creative. The data is unambiguous: Reels convert, text posts don't.
• Test scaling Reel winners with incremental budget (€50-100/day) before committing large spend — Merlene proved the concept at €24, now validate at scale.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all static 'Bericht' format ads immediately — €274 spent with literally zero purchases is not a sample size problem, it's a format problem.
• Kill event/announcement ads ('XXL STOCK SALE!', 'Feestelijke opening') — these are organic content, not paid conversion drivers.
• Stop scaling Reel Mary-Lynn — at 0.41x ROAS it's destroying margin; diagnose what's different vs. Merlene before spending another euro.
